notes.compendium_scope: Writing-class compendiums (eval_classes containing writing): check_writing.md, check_student_facing.md, check_prompts.md, check_sales_copy.md, check_strategy_tie_in.md. check_prompts.md gets one representative N/A entry rather than all 44 — this file has zero fenced prompt blocks or {{prompt:}} markers (it is pure exposition, never asks the student to paste anything), so the compendium's entire scope (copy-this affordance) is out of play, and 44 near-identical N/A rows would be a coverage-ledger checkbox exercise rather than evidence. check_sales_copy.md and check_strategy_tie_in.md get full per-rule coverage (all N/A) because both compendiums' firing surfaces (buyer-facing copy; Big Idea/Mood/Key Concepts) are cleanly absent rather than partially present, matching the fuller-coverage precedent in ae101--exercise--compound-and-close.writing.json.
notes.rule20_count_adjacency_open_question: check_writing.md §20 bans a numeral sitting adjacent to the list it counts (drift risk when the list changes). Line 5's 'Six levels, from assistance to a system you keep improving' sits above six ## H2 sections. Read against the scroll layout, this looks like the banned adjacent-count shape. But the maintainer block commits Part 1 to one slide per level (Antti-directed 2026-08-14) — in the Slides rendering the six items are never simultaneously visible with the numeral, which is exactly §20's stated carve-out test ('does the numeral appear where the items are NOT visible? Yes → keep it'). Landed on PASS because the file is deliberately dual-rendered and the slide-mode reading is the one the maintainer block explicitly designed for, but flagging the reasoning since a scroll-only read would call this a violation.
notes.worktree_earning_open_question: check_student_facing.md §2 (earn every technical term) / §14 (don't plant jargon too early): line 31 uses 'Worktrees separate the changes...' unearned. This file is the FIRST of four items in getting-going.md's Pre-reads before Module 2 list; the item that actually earns 'worktree' (the Multi-session and Git reference) sits two items later in the same list. Scored PASS rather than REVISE because git worktrees are ordinary professional vocabulary for the AE101 engineer audience (check_student_facing.md §2's 'ordinary professional vocabulary...just use it' carve-out, same reasoning as the done-done precedent) and the sentence reads clearly even without prior git-worktree knowledge. Flagging because the read-order argument (this file lands before the earning reference) is a real, if minor, ordering question a maintainer might want to settle explicitly.
